title.en: Women Like Valiant Men: The Amazons of Chugara
title.zh: 如勇男般的女子:丘加拉的亞馬遜

region.en: Chugara, province of the Canas (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 卡納斯省丘加拉(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: They affirm of a certainty that, after that powerful captain arose in Hatuncollao, there appeared in the province of the Canas, which lies between the Canches and Collao, near the village called Chugara, some women who were like valiant men. Taking up arms they subdued those who were in the district where they lived, and, almost like what is told of the Amazons, they made homes for themselves, without husbands. These people, after this had gone on for some years, and they had performed some famous deeds, came to fight with Zapana, he who had become Lord of Hatuncollao; and to defend themselves against his power, which was great, they made fortresses and walls, which still exist. But after they had done all to the utmost of their power, they were taken and killed, and their name disappeared.
summary.zh: 據說確有其事:繼哈通科利亞奧那位強大的酋長崛起之後,在卡納斯省——坎切斯與科利亞奧之間——的丘加拉村附近,出現了一批勇武如男子的女子。她們執兵而戰,征服了所居之地的居民;幾乎如傳說中的亞馬遜,她們自立門戶,不嫁不婚。數年之間,她們建立功業,聲名遠播,竟至與哈通科利亞奧之主薩帕納交鋒;為抗其強權,她們築起堡壘與城牆——至今猶存。然而她們雖竭盡全力,終被擒殺,其名自此湮沒無聞。

sensitivity.note: The land-of-women topos grounded in named ruins; Cieza records it from witnesses who visited the site.

title.en: The Sun Shining Very Brightly Came Forth from the Island of Titicaca
title.zh: 太陽燦然出自的的喀喀島

region.en: Island of Titicaca, lake of the Collao (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 科利亞奧大湖的的喀喀島(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: Before the Incas reigned in these kingdoms, or had ever been heard of, the Indians relate another thing much more notable than all things else that they say. For they declare that they were a long time without seeing the sun, and that, suffering much evil from its absence, great prayers and vows were offered up to their gods, imploring for the light they needed. Things being in this state, the sun, shining very brightly, came forth from the island of Titicaca, in the great lake of the Collao, at which every one rejoiced.
summary.zh: 早在印加人稱王、甚至無人聽說過印加之前,印第安人還講著一件比一切傳說更著名的事。他們說:曾經很長時間看不見太陽,因太陽缺席而受盡苦難,便向他們的神極力祈禱、許願,哀求賜下所需的光明。就在此時,太陽燦然生輝,從科利亞奧大湖的的喀喀島上噴薄而出——眾人皆大歡喜。

sensitivity.note: Cieza's version of the sun-emergence: darkness-then-light, no creator sequence included - a minimal solar theogony.

title.en: The White Man of Great Stature Who Made Water Flow from Stones
title.zh: 身量高大的白人:點石出水者

region.en: Roads of the mountains to the sea coast (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 山路至海濱(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: Presently afterwards, they say, there came from a southern direction a white man of great stature, who, by his aspect and presence, called forth great veneration and obedience. This man who thus appeared had great power, insomuch that he could change plains into mountains, and great hills into valleys, and make water flow out of stones. As soon as such power was beheld, the people called him the Maker of created things, the Prince of all things, Father of the Sun. For they say that he performed other wonders, giving life to men and animals, so that by his hand marvellous great benefits were conferred on the people. Such was the story that the Indians who told it to me say that they heard from their ancestors, who in like manner heard it in the old songs which they received from very ancient times. They say that this man went on towards the north, working these marvels along the way of the mountains; and that he never more returned so as to be seen. In many places he gave orders to men how they should live, and he spoke lovingly to them and with much gentleness, admonishing them that they should do good, and no evil or injury one to another, and that they should be loving and charitable to all. In most parts he is generally called Ticiviracocha, but in the province of the Collao they call him Tuapaca, and in other places Arnauan. In many parts they built temples in which they put blocks of stone in likeness of him, and offered up sacrifices before them. It is held that the great blocks at Tiahuanacu were from that time.
summary.zh: 此後不久——相傳——自南方來了一位身量高大的白人,儀表威嚴,令人望之生敬、順服。此人神力無邊:他能把平原變作高山,把崇嶺夷為深谷,能點石而出泉。人們見此神威,便稱他為「造物之主」「萬有之王」「太陽之父」。相傳他還行過別樣奇事:使男子與畜類復生,親手降下莫大恩惠於人民。向我講述此事的印第安人說,這故事是他們從祖先那裡聽來的,而祖先又是從極古的歌謠中傳承下來的。相傳此人繼續北上,沿著山路一路顯聖;此後再未現身。他在許多地方教人如何生活,言語溫存柔和,勸人行善,勿相互傷害,當彼此仁愛、施惠於人。各地對他稱呼不一:多稱「提基維拉科查」,科利亞省稱「圖阿帕卡」,另一些地方稱「阿爾瑙安」。許多地方為他建廟,廟中供上狀似其形的石塊,在其前獻祭。人們說,蒂亞瓦納科的巨石便是那個時代留下來的。

sensitivity.note: Cieza's white culture-hero heard in the old songs; the apostle speculation is his own editorial frame.

title.en: The Fire from Heaven at Cacha, and the Mantle That Entered the Waves

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: They say that, a long time having passed, they again saw another man resembling the first, whose name they do not mention; but they received it from their forefathers as very certain that wherever this personage came and there were sick, he healed them, and where there were blind he gave them sight by only uttering words. Through acts so good and useful he was much beloved by all. In this fashion, working great things by his words, he arrived at the province of the Canas, in which, near to a village which has the name of Cacha, the people rose against him, threatening to stone him. They saw him upon his knees, with his hands raised to heaven, as if invoking the divine favour to liberate him from the danger that threatened him. Presently there appeared a great fire in the heaven, which they thought to be surrounding them. Full of fear and trembling, they came to him whom they had wanted to kill, and with loud clamour besought him to be pleased to forgive them. For they knew that this punishment threatened them because of the sin they had committed in wishing to stone the stranger. Presently they saw that when he ordered the fire to cease, it was extinguished, so that they were themselves witnesses of what had come to pass; and the stones were consumed and burnt up in such wise as that large blocks could be lifted in the hand, as if they were of cork. Leaving the place where these things happened, the man arrived on the sea coast, where, holding his mantle, he went in amongst the waves and was never more seen. And as he went, so they gave him the name of Viracocha, which means 'the foam of the sea.' Soon afterwards they made a temple in this village of Cacha, on the other side of a river which passes near, where they set up an idol of stone, very large, but in a somewhat narrow recess. Some gold was found in holes near it. Whether this or any other was intended for one of the glorious apostles who, in the days of his preaching, had passed this way, God Almighty knows.
summary.zh: 相傳良久之後,他們又見到一位與前者相像的人;其名不傳。但祖先們確鑿相告:此人每到之處,病者得愈,盲者一聞其言便得復明。他善行廣布,深得眾愛。他以言語創行大事,行至卡納斯省,在卡查村附近,當地人群起欲以石擊之。眾人見他屈膝跪地,雙手向天,似在祈求上蒼解其危難。霎時間,天現大火,彷彿要將他們團團圍住。眾人戰慄恐懼,紛紛來到方才欲殺之人面前,大聲哀求饒恕——他們明白:這懲罰是因他們欲以石擊客人之罪而降。隨後,那人一聲令下,天火頓熄;眾人親眼所見:石塊盡被燒枯,燒得如此輕盈,大石竟可單手舉起,輕如木栓。那人離開此地,行至海濱,展其氅衣,步入波濤,從此不再現身。他如此離去,人們便稱他為「維拉科查」——意即「海之泡沫」。不久,卡查村便在近旁河對岸建起一座神廟,供上一尊極大的石像,安置於略顯狹窄的壁龕之中;像旁洞穴曾掘得黃金。至於這尊石像或其他,是否為昔日傳道途中經此的某位榮耀使徒,唯有全能的上帝知曉。

sensitivity.note: Cieza's Cacha fire parallels Sarmiento's and Salcamayhua's versions; the apostle speculation is quoted as editorial.

title.en: Worse than Supais: The Name Viracocha Given and Taken Back
title.zh: 比魔鬼還壞:維拉科查之名的予與奪

region.zh: 庫斯科科里坎查(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: Treating of this name Viracocha, I wish to disabuse the reader of the popular belief that the natives called the Spaniards by the name of Viracocha, which means foam of the sea. So far as the word is concerned it is true, for vira is the word for grease, and cocha is the sea. And seeing that the Spaniards came by sea, that name has been attributed to them. But this is a wrong interpretation, according to the explanation which I received at Cuzco, and which the Orejones give. They say that before Atahuallpa was taken prisoner by the Spaniards in the province of Caxamarca, there had been great wars between him and his brother Huascar Inca... While these passions were at their height, Atahuallpa had been made prisoner and had agreed with Pizarro to give him a house of gold as his ransom. Martin Bueno, Zarate, and Moguer went to Cuzco to receive it, the greater part being in the Sun temple called Curicancha. As these Christians arrived at Cuzco at the time when the party of Huascar was suffering under the above calamity, the oppressed Yncas rejoiced when they heard of the imprisonment of Atahuallpa, and with great supplications implored the aid of the Christians against their enemy, declaring that they must be sent by the intervention of their great God Ticiviracocha, and that they were his sons; and presently they called them so, giving them the name of Viracocha. They ordered the High Priest and the other ministers of the temple to keep the sacred women there... As these Spaniards were so free from all restraint, and held the honor of the people so lightly, in return for the hospitality and friendliness with which they were received, they corrupted some of the virgins; which was the reason that the Indians, who also saw how little reverence the Spaniards felt for the Sun, and how shamelessly and without the fear of God they violated the mamaconas, which the Indians held to be a great sacrilege, began to say that such people were not sons of God, but that they were worse than Supais, which is their name of Devil. Nevertheless... the name of Viracocha continued from that day.
summary.zh: 說到「維拉科查」這個名字,我要澄清世俗的誤解:人們以為土人因「維拉科查」意為「海之泡沫」(維拉=油脂,科查=海),而西班牙人自海上而來,故以此名稱呼他們。但據我在庫斯科從「耳垂貴胄」處所得的解釋,這是錯誤的。他們說:阿塔瓦爾帕在卡哈馬卡被西班牙人擒獲之前,他與兄弟瓦伊斯卡爾·印加之間已爆發大戰……瓦伊斯卡爾在阿普里馬克河的科塔班巴隘口被查爾庫奇馬生擒,備受凌虐;基斯-基斯在庫斯科大肆屠戮,殺死瓦伊斯卡爾三十位兄弟。正當此際,阿塔瓦爾帕被擒,與皮薩羅約定以一屋黃金贖身。馬丁·布埃諾、薩拉特與莫格雷奉命赴庫斯科收取贖金——大部分藏於名為科里坎查的太陽神廟。受壓迫的印加人聞知阿塔瓦爾帕被擒,大喜過望,苦苦哀求基督徒相助對敵,聲稱他們必是偉大的神提基維拉科查所遣、是他的兒子們——於是便稱他們為「維拉科查」。然而這些西班牙人毫無忌憚,視他人榮譽如糞土:受人殷勤款待,卻姦污了部分守廟的聖女;印第安人又親見他們對太陽何等輕慢,竟恬不知恥、不畏神明地玷污了瑪瑪庫納——在印第安人看來,這是滔天瀆神。於是人們開始說:這些人絕非神之子,而是比「蘇帕伊」——他們稱魔鬼為蘇帕伊——還要壞的東西。但「維拉科查」之名,卻自那日起沿用至今。

title.en: Slings of Gold: Six Ancestors in the House of Production
title.zh: 金彈弓:生產之屋的六位先祖

region.zh: 帕卡雷克-坦波(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: When all the races who lived in these regions were in a state of disorder, slaughtering each other and sunk in vice, there appeared three men and three women in a place not far from the city of Cuzco, which is called Pacarec Tampu - the House of Production. The men who came forth from there were, as they relate, the one Ayar Ucho, and the other Ayar Cachi Asauca, and the other they say was named Ayar Manco. Of the women, one had the name of Mama Huaco, the other Mama Cora, the other Mama Rahua. They say that these people came forth dressed in long mantles, and some vestments like a shirt without collar or sleeves, made of very fine wool, with patterns of different kinds, which they called tacapu - 'vestures of kings'. And each of these lords held in the hand a sling of gold with a stone in it. The women came out dressed very richly like the men, and they had much gold. One of the brothers named Ayar Uchu spoke to his brethren that they should make a beginning of the great things that they had to do; for their presumption was such that they thought they were to make themselves sole lords of the land. They were determined to form in that place a new settlement, to which they gave the name of Pacarec Tampu. They say that one of the three, named Ayar Cachi, was so valiant and had such great power, that, with stones hurled from his sling, he split the hills and threw them up to the clouds. When the other brothers saw this they were sorry, thinking that it was an affront to them who could not do such things, and they were enraged by reason of their envy. Then they asked him sweetly and with gentle words, though full of deceit, to return and enter the mouth of a cave where they had their treasure, to bring out a certain vase of gold that they had forgotten. Ayar Cachi, believing that there was no deceit in what his brother said, joyfully went to do what they required of him, but he had scarcely got into the cave when the other two so filled the mouth up with stones that it could not be seen. This done, they relate for a certainty that the earth trembled in such a manner that many hills fell into the valleys. Afterwards, when the Indians exalted them with grand titles, they were called Ancha hatun apu intipchuri! which means 'Oh very great lord, child of the sun.'
summary.zh: 當各地族群陷入混亂、自相殘殺、沉溺於罪惡之際,庫斯科城外不遠處,名為「帕卡雷克-坦普」(意即「生產之屋」)的地方,出現了三男三女。相傳男子三人為:亞亞爾-烏丘、亞亞爾-卡奇-阿薩烏卡、亞亞爾-曼科;女子三人為:瑪瑪·瓦科、瑪瑪·科拉、瑪瑪·拉瓦。相傳他們走出時,身披長氅,內著領口無袖、極細羊毛織就、花紋各異的上衣,名「塔卡普」——意即「王者之衣」。每位主子手中各執一把嵌石的金彈弓。女子們的服飾與男子一樣華貴,且攜帶大量黃金。兄弟之一亞亞爾-烏丘對眾兄弟說:該開創大業了——他們的自負,竟以為自己注定要做天下唯一的主。他們決定就地建一新聚落,名為帕卡雷克-坦普。相傳亞亞爾-卡奇勇猛絕倫、神力蓋世:彈弓擲石,劈山碎嶺,能把石塊擲上雲端。眾兄弟見狀心中不快——自愧弗如,妒火中燒。他們便甜言蜜語、滿懷詭計地請他回到藏寶的洞穴,取出遺忘的金瓶。亞亞爾-卡奇信以為真,欣然前往;他剛一進洞,兩位兄弟便用石頭把洞口塞得嚴嚴實實。相傳此舉之後,大地猛烈震動,許多山頭塌入谷中。後來印第安人以顯赫尊號稱頌他們:「安查·哈通·阿普·因蒂普丘里!」——啊,極偉大的主,太陽之子!

sensitivity.note: Cieza's six-ancestor version with Mama Cora and Mama Rahua; the earth-tremor at the sealing differs from Sarmiento's narrative.

passages.text: When all the races who lived in these regions were in a state of disorder, slaughtering each other and sunk in vice, there appeared three men and three women in a place not far from the city of Cuzco, which is called Pacarec Tampu. And according to the interpretation, Pacarec Tampu is as much as to say the House of Production.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Cieza de León, Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, ch. 6 (Markham 1883); not verbatim.

passages.text: They say that these people came forth, dressed in long mantles, and some vestments like a shirt without collar or sleeves, made of very fine wool, with patterns of different kinds, which they called tacapu, and in our language the meaning is 'vestures of kings.' And each of these lords held in the hand a sling of gold with a stone in it.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Cieza de León, Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, ch. 6 (Markham 1883); not verbatim.

passages.text: One of the three, named Ayar Cachi, was so valiant and had such great power, that, with stones hurled from his sling, he split the hills and threw them up to the clouds. When the other brothers saw this they were sorry... and they were enraged by reason of their envy. Then they asked him sweetly and with gentle words, though full of deceit, to return and enter the mouth of a cave where they had their treasure, to bring out a certain vase of gold... Ayar Cachi, believing that there was no deceit in what his brother said, joyfully went to do what they required of him, but he had scarcely got into the cave when the other two so filled the mouth up with stones that it could not be seen. This done, they relate for a certainty that the earth trembled in such a manner that many hills fell into the valleys.
passages.note: Condensed paraphrase of Cieza de León, Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, ch. 6 (Markham 1883); not verbatim.

texts.canonical_translation: Sir Clements Markham, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru (Hakluyt Society, 1883)

title.en: Ayar Cachi Comes with Wings: 'Your Ears Shall Be Bored as You Behold in Mine'
title.zh: 羽翼的亞亞爾-卡奇:「爾等穿耳,如我所戴」

region.zh: 瓜納考雷山(瓦納考里)(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: After the two Incas had settled in Tampu Quiru, careless now about seeing Ayar Cachi again, they beheld him coming in the air with great wings of coloured feathers, and they, by reason of the great fear that this visit caused them, wanted to flee away; but he quickly removed their terror by saying to them: 'Do not fear, neither be afflicted; for I only come that the empire of the Incas may begin to be known. Wherefore leave this settlement that you have made, and advance further down until you see a valley, and there found the Cuzco, which will be of great note. For here are only hamlets, and of little importance; but that will be a great city, where the sumptuous temple must be built that will be so honoured and frequented, and where the sun will be so worshipped. I shall remain in the form and fashion that you will see on a hill not distant from here; and will be for you and your descendants a place of sanctity and worship, and its name shall be Guanacaure. And in return for the good things that you will have received from me, I pray that you will always adore me as God, and set up altars in that place, at which to offer sacrifices. If you do this, you shall receive help from me in war; and as a sign that from henceforward you are to be esteemed, honoured, and feared, your ears shall be bored in the manner that you now behold in mine.' And when he had so spoken they say that he appeared with ear ornaments of gold set round as with a gem. The brothers, astonished at what they saw, were as men struck dumb; when their perturbation had ceased, they replied that they were content to do as he commanded, and presently they went in haste to the hill called the Hill of Guanacaure, which from that time forward was accounted sacred. The Orejones further say that the practice of assuming the fringe and of arming the knights began here.
summary.zh: 兩兄弟定居坦普-基魯之後,已不再掛念亞亞爾-卡奇。忽然,他們望見他憑著絢麗羽翼的大翅膀從空中而來。二人嚇得魂飛魄散,幾欲逃命;他卻迅即為他們除去恐懼,說道:「不要害怕,也不要憂愁;我來,只為使印加帝國自此聞名。離開你們建立的這個聚落,往下走,直到望見一處谷地,在那裡建立庫斯科——它必成大城。此地不過是小村陋巷,微不足道;那裡卻要建起豪華的神廟,受人尊崇,香火鼎盛,太陽將在那裡受萬民敬拜。我將留驻在這不遠處山丘上——你們會看見我的形貌;我與我的子孫將成為你們的聖所與崇拜之地,其名為瓜納考雷。作為你們受我恩惠的回報,我求你們永遠奉我如神,在彼處設壇獻祭。若能如此,戰時我必佑助你們;為記你們從此當受尊崇、敬仰與敬畏,你們要像我這樣穿耳——如你們現在所見。」言畢,相傳他顯出鑲嵌寶石般的金耳飾。兄弟們驚訝得說不出話來;心神稍定,便答應遵命而行,急忙趕往那座自此被奉為聖地的瓜納考雷山。耳垂貴胄們說:戴王纓、封騎士之禮,便自此而始。

sensitivity.note: Cieza's winged-escape variant of Ayar Cachi/Huanacaure; Cieza equates Ayar Cachi with the hill's name and preserves the ear-boring charter.

title.en: The Fast of Zaziy: Straw-Gathering and Four Woven Dresses
title.zh: 扎西齋戒:拾草與一日四衣

region.zh: 瓜納考雷山(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by Cieza de León, publ. Markham trans. 1883 (Second Part)

source.work: Pedro de Cieza de León, The Second Part of the Chronicle of Peru, trans. and ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1883

summary.en: It would seem that these lords arranged the ceremony for assuming the fringe or crown, and they say that Ayar Cachi dressed in the same manner, on this same hill of Guanacaure. He who was to become Inca was dressed, on one day, in a black shirt painted with red patterns and no collar, and on his head a fawn-coloured plait twisted round. And he wore a long grey mantle, in which dress he came forth from his lodging and went into the fields to gather a wisp of straw, and he had to stay out all day doing this, without eating or drinking, for it was his duty to fast. And the mother and sisters of the former Inca had to remain spinning with such diligence that, during that one day, they had to spin and weave four dresses, fasting all the time: one of these dresses consisted of a grey shirt and white mantle, and another had to be all white, and the other had to be blue, with cords and trimmings. He who was to become Inca had to wear these dresses, and to fast for the appointed time, which is one month, and they call this fast zaziy.
summary.zh: 看來,王纓加冕之禮便是由這些先王定下的;相傳亞亞爾-卡奇也在瓜納考雷山上如此更衣。將立為印加王者,首日須著無領紅紋黑衫,頭繞鹿色髮辮,外披灰色長氅;如此裝束出門,下田拾取一束稻草,整日在外,不得飲食——齋戒是他的本分。先王之母與姊妹們則須勤奮紡織:就在這一日之內,紡織出四套衣服,且終日不得進食:一套灰衫白氅,一套純白,一套藍色帶繩飾。將立為王者須依次穿著這些衣服,並齋戒滿一個月——此齋名為「扎西」。

sensitivity.note: The investiture fast with its exact dress sequence; a rare liturgical detail from the Orejone informants.
